thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high GPU queue growth in eu-west-1 (service=runtime, severity=high) — paging oncall@eng-sre
Emma O'Neill: I'm on it, acked the pager. seeing queue spike in metric dashboard (eu-west-1/gpu-pool-a)
Emma O'Neill: queue length ~ 4800 requests, accepted rate stalled ~ 400 r/s, tokens/sec down 45%
Raj Patel: same, autoscaler target tried to add nodes but provider returned repeated 429s and then quotaExceeded on 3rd attempt
Maria Gomez: recalling last deploy? any config change to autoscaler policies?
Dave Li: no infra change in last 24h. provider side reports API throttling in that region — opening ticket with provider support now.
Emma O'Neill: can we surface which customers impacted? Sam from CS — can you pull customer pulse? @Sam Chen (CS)
Sam Chen (CS): already flagged two higher-traffic customers seeing errors: corp-alpha and beta-ads. Support ticket IDs #6789 #6790. Customers seeing 503/429 from our API.
Support Bot: Automated note: 503 spikes start 2026-03-15T02:14:10Z, peak 02:17:42Z, correlated with queue backlog.
Raj Patel: trying fallback policy: route requests to smaller `mix-lite` model variant to shed GPU memory, initiating rollout to 10% for non-enterprise keys
Emma O'Neill: rollouts started — pushing redirect rules now.
Raj Patel: patch applied: router rule `if queue_depth > 2000 then variant = mix-lite` — sending config
Maria Gomez: we need to slow ingest too — enabling rate limiter at edge to 800 r/s for public keys, and enable per-customer throt for corp-alpha/beta-ads to 50 r/s each
Emma O'Neill: rate limits in place. queue growth rate slowed but still long tail, autoscaler still failing because provider API returns 429 with `retry-after` 90s.
Dave Li: provider engagement: support responded — they are rate-limiting our autoscale requests due to sudden spike and internal quota guard. They gave a temporary exception but advised to batch scale calls.
Raj Patel: changed our autoscaler to `batch_scale=true` and exponential backoff; also enabling local overcommit of small T4 nodes to accept some traffic while larger nodes are provisioned
Ana Torres: coordinating with oncall in other regions to failover some traffic to us-east-1 if needed. how much cross-region latency impact?
Emma O'Neill: measured added 120-180ms p90 for those routed, acceptable for some customers. set failover for non-SLA keys only.
Sam Chen (CS): informed corp-alpha that we're throttling but routing some of their requests; they reported degraded quality but service still returns answers for low-priority traffic.
Support Bot: Incident timeline note appended: root cause = provider autoscale throttling + sudden traffic ramp from marketing campaign; mitigation = routing to smaller models, edge rate-limiting, batch-scale change, temporary exception from provider.
Maria Gomez: temporary mitigations applied. we should capture action items: 1) add autoscaler batching + jitter (short-term patch) 2) cross-region failover playbook refinement 3) per-customer dynamic throttles by priority keys 4) provider escalation / higher quota request 5) improve alerting to include provider 429s in autoscale path
Raj Patel: also propose adding local capacity reservation for burst windows (pre-warm small nodes) and a circuit-breaker that can instantly switch to `mix-lite` for non-SLA keys when queue > 1500
Dave Li: I'll own provider quota escalation and temporary quota increase request. ticket ref: PROVIDER-5421. ETA for long-term quota: 3w (unconfirmed).
Emma O'Neill: Maria, can you drive the postmortem doc? List of facts, timeline, mitigations, and blameless action items. We need a follow-up runbook for similar events.
Maria Gomez: will start doc in #incidents-docs and ping everyone for edits. initial draft due EOD today.
Ana Torres: proposed immediate action: schedule a run of synthetic load test with autoscaler enabled to reproduce provider throttling scenario in staging.
Raj Patel: test plan: spike to 20k concurrent queue for 15m, observe autoscale behavior; validate batch_scale flag and fallback routing. Will run tomorrow 03:00 UTC in staging.
Emma O'Neill: After mitigations we observed queue down to ~120, accepted rate normalized. marking incident as contained at 02:46Z.
Incident Bot: Incident update: severity downgraded to medium — customer errors reduced below threshold.
Sam Chen (CS): follow-up: corp-alpha wants SLA credits discussion. logged customer escalation to account team.
Support Bot: Created follow-up ticket: PM-2345 for postmortem + customer comms.
Maria Gomez: Action items (owner / due):
- Maria: Create postmortem doc + timeline (due EOD today)
- Raj: Autoscaler batching + jitter PR + unit tests (due 5 business days)
- Dave: Provider quota escalation + confirm temporary exception (due 48h)
- Ana: Cross-region failover playbook update + test plan (due 7 days)
- Emma: Customer impact summary + coordinate CS comms (due 24h)
- Support: Add alerts for autoscale 429s and provider-side errors (due 3 days)
Emma O'Neill: thanks everyone. will run handoff to next oncall at 03:15Z. if anybody adds anything to the doc, ping me. :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: pushing first autoscaler batching PR now, will @Emma when merged.
Maria Gomez: Draft posted: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PM-2345 (doc link) — please add lane notes.
Support Bot: Note: next steps scheduled: postmortem review meeting 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC.
Emma O'Neill: Handoff complete to next oncall (Ana). leaving channel.
Ana Torres: ack and taking over monitoring for the night. will escalate if anything changes.
Incident Bot: Thread closed by Emma O'Neill at 03:20Z (auto-noted).
